name: Question 8
problem:
$$
{y}^{″}+3y=f(x),\,y(0)=5,\,{y}^{′}(0)=0
$$

Consider the initial value problem above, where $f(x)$ is an even, $2\pi $-periodic function. Select the missing part in the solution of the IVP, where the second infinite sum on the right-hand side below represents a particular solution of the differential equation.

$$
y(x)∼{{field-1}}+{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)
$$
worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of a linear differential equation of the form ${y}^{″}+{\omega }^{2}y=f(x)$ is given by $y={y}_{c}+{y}_{p},$ where ${y}_{c}$ is the solution to the homogeneous equation and ${y}_{p}$ is a particular solution.

First, we address the particular solution ${y}_{p}.$ Since $f(x)$ is an even function and the differential operator contains no ${y}^{′}$ (damping) term, the particular solution inherits the symmetry and is also an even function consisting only of cosine terms. This is represented by the term

$$
{y}_{p}(x)={\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx).
$$

Next, we find the homogeneous solution. The characteristic equation ${\lambda }^{2}+3=0$ gives roots $\lambda =\pm \sqrt{3}\text{i}.$ So, we have

$$
{y}_{c}=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{3}x)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{3}x).
$$

To find the unknown constants, we apply the initial conditions. Differentiating the total solution gives

$$
{y}^{′}(x)∼-A\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{3}x)+B\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{3}x)-{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx).
$$

Using the derivative condition ${y}^{′}(0)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(0) & =-A\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)+B\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)-{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(0) \\ 0 & =0+B\sqrt{3}-0 \\ B & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Note that because the total solution is an even function, its derivative is an odd function, which must vanish at $x=0.$

Next, we use the condition $y(0)=5.$ With $B=0,$ the total solution is

$$
y(x)∼A\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{3}x)+{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx).
$$

Applying $y(0)=5$ and noting that $\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)=1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}5 & =A+{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n} \\ A & =5-{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $A$ back into ${y}_{c}=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{3}x),$ we find the missing part:

$$
y(x)∼\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{3}x)(5-{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n})+{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)
$$

Question 8

y″+3y=f(x),y(0)=5,y′(0)=0 Consider the initial value problem above, where f(x) is an even, 2π-periodic function. Select the missing part in the solution of the IVP, where the second infinite sum on the right-hand side below represents a particular solution of the differential equation.
cos⁡(3x)(5−∑n=0∞an)
sin⁡(3x)(5−∑n=0∞an)
cos⁡(3x)(∑n=0∞an−5)
cos⁡(3x)(5+∑n=0∞an)
cos⁡(3x)(5−∑n=0∞an)
y(x)∼{(sin⁡(3x)(5−∑n=0∞an))(S0)}+∑n=0∞ancos⁡(nx)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that the general solution of a linear differential equation of the form y″+ω2y=f(x) is given by y=yc+yp, where yc is the solution to the homogeneous equation and yp is a particular solution.

First, we address the particular solution yp. Since f(x) is an even function and the differential operator contains no y′ (damping) term, the particular solution inherits the symmetry and is also an even function consisting only of cosine terms. This is represented by the term yp(x)=∑n=0∞ancos⁡(nx).

Next, we find the homogeneous solution. The characteristic equation λ2+3=0 gives roots λ=±3i. So, we have yc=Acos⁡(3x)+Bsin⁡(3x).

To find the unknown constants, we apply the initial conditions. Differentiating the total solution gives y′(x)∼−A3sin⁡(3x)+B3cos⁡(3x)−∑n=1∞nansin⁡(nx). Using the derivative condition y′(0)=0: y′(0)=−A3sin⁡(0)+B3cos⁡(0)−∑n=1∞nansin⁡(0)0=0+B3−0B=0 Note that because the total solution is an even function, its derivative is an odd function, which must vanish at x=0.

Next, we use the condition y(0)=5. With B=0, the total solution is y(x)∼Acos⁡(3x)+∑n=0∞ancos⁡(nx).

Applying y(0)=5 and noting that cos⁡(0)=1, we have 5=A+∑n=0∞anA=5−∑n=0∞an.

Substituting A back into yc=Acos⁡(3x), we find the missing part: y(x)∼cos⁡(3x)(5−∑n=0∞an)+∑n=0∞ancos⁡(nx)
